concerns.text: Task T011e defers the insertion of IRB-approved text to a manual step without a corresponding automated verification gate in the code. This violates Constitution Principle VI (Participant Ethics) and Spec US0, which require that an approved protocol exists and is enforced before data collection. The task list fails to preserve the constraint that the system must be 'Production Ready' only when the text is present, leaving a legal/ethical gap.

Tasks T022b_1 and T022b split IP extraction and session rejection into two steps where T022b has no implementation artifact. This creates a semantic weakening of the Spec US1 requirement for 'hashed IP' and security. The rejection logic is described but not concretely delivered as a verified code block, risking a failure to enforce the 'No PII' and 'Security' constraints defined in the Spec and Constitution.

Tasks T024a and T024b (Preprocess and Execute) are marked incomplete, leaving the 'cleaned_data.csv' artifact missing. This violates the Spec US2 requirement for a Repeated-Measures ANOVA pipeline, as the analysis scripts (T025a, T027a) depend on this wide-format artifact. The task list fails to preserve the constraint that the analysis pipeline must be executable.

Task T046a (Power Analysis) is incomplete and relies on missing mock data (T043a). This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which mandates that all results be reproducible by re-running code against data. The task list does not ensure the fixed seed and schema requirements are met, creating a gap in the reproducibility constraint.

Tasks T022d (real-time duplicate flagging) and T028d (post-hoc duplicate detection) introduce redundant logic that contradicts the Spec US1 and Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene). The Spec requires a single source of truth for data integrity; having two conflicting mechanisms for duplicate detection risks race conditions and data inconsistency, weakening the data hygiene constraint.
